haiku-low.q1: There is no difference in the response. Both get HTTP 401 with "Invalid email or password". For an unknown email, the password check still runs against a dummy hash, so timing does not reveal the account.
haiku-low.q2: The server returns HTTP 429 with "Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." without a password check. The refused request is not recorded as a failure.
haiku-low.q3: The existing session named by the incoming sid cookie is deleted in the same transaction as the new session insert, whether or not it is still valid.
haiku-low.q4: Only the raw random session ID, with no user data. The cookie is set HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: Idle timeout does not apply while requests continue, since each valid request resets last_seen_at. The session stops working 12 hours after login, at expires_at.
haiku-low.q6: It clears the sid cookie and redirects the browser to /login. It serves no page.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the matching sessions row before replying, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone or no cookie was sent, the result is the same.
haiku-low.q8: In the shared Postgres database. Any instance finds it by looking up the row whose session ID hash matches the cookie's hash.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table in Postgres, one row per failed attempt with attempted_at. The server counts this email's rows whose attempted_at falls within 10 minutes before now.
haiku-low.q10: It compares the cookie's hash to a row with expires_at later than now and last_seen_at later than now minus 30 minutes. If valid, it writes last_seen_at as now and returns user_id.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 login page: "Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again shortly." No cookie is set and nothing is changed, because the transaction is all or nothing.
haiku-low.q12: The cleanup timer in each app instance, running every 10 minutes, deletes sessions past expires_at or idle more than 30 minutes.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ. Both get HTTP 401 with the login page and "Invalid email or password". For an unknown email the password is checked against a dummy hash, so timing is similar.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked, so the login gets a 429 login page ("Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.") without a password check. The attempt is not recorded as a failure and does not extend the lock. (The 5th failure itself still got a 401.)
sonnet.q3: The session named by the incoming sid cookie is deleted, whether or not it is still valid. It is deleted in the same transaction that inserts the new session with a new random ID.
sonnet.q4: Only the raw random session ID, with no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
sonnet.q5: 12 hours after login (absolute timeout), even though the user is active. Activity keeps the idle timeout (30 minutes) from firing, but the session ends at expires_at.
sonnet.q6: It clears the sid cookie and redirects (302) to /login.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie was sent, the server deletes the sessions row whose hash matches, before replying. Then it clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone or there is no cookie, the result is the same.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres database, in the sessions table, keyed by the SHA-256 hash of the session ID. Either instance hashes the sid cookie's ID and looks up the row in Postgres.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table (email, attempted_at), one row per failed attempt. The server counts that email's rows where attempted_at is within the last 10 minutes from now. (The exact comparison is not spelled out beyond that.)
sonnet.q10: It compares timestamps in one UPDATE: expires_at is later than now, and last_seen_at is later than now minus 30 minutes, on the row matching the cookie's hash. When valid, it sets last_seen_at to now and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 login page: "Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again shortly." No cookie is set and nothing is changed.
sonnet.q12: Cleanup. It runs in each app instance every 10 minutes and deletes sessions past expires_at or idle for more than 30 minutes. Expired sessions are also refused on every request regardless of cleanup.
